chapter_theme: From the gross to the subtle. The great path leads to a round city where nada sounds, the presence of the Lord; past the three voids are three lights whose circle is the chakra, the nose-tip is the suzhumunai, the guru Nandi sits in the fire-circle at the brow where sun and moon stand, and nada-bindu is the source of body and life. Then the practice: A at the kundalini breath, the second letter at the throat, M at the whirl; puraka thirty-two, kumbhaka double, rechaka sixteen; in by the left and out by pingala, kept from full moon to new; fire raised by the breath, nectar fed above the whirl, kechari and the root Ganapati; the five letters as five gods; the maiden's three unsayable letters that make life; initiation as the Siva-chakra with the goddess's letter at its centre; and in place of toddy and ganja the Soma-nectar, drunk with the Lord of the hall in a song of advaita.
structure_note: 2568 to 2572 give the path and its summit (gross to subtle, the city of nada, the three lights, nose-tip and brow); 2573 to 2577 nada-bindu, guru Nandi, the blissful place and the 1,008-petalled seat; 2578 to 2584 the breath practice (letters, counts, channels, fortnight, fire and nectar, kechari); 2585 to 2589 the five letters, the maiden's three letters and initiation; 2590 to 2592 nectar against intoxicants and the advaita song. Seven stanzas (2576, 2577, 2579, 2583, 2590, 2592, and 2591 in its first half) end in கும்மியடியுங்கடி, 'dance the kummi, girls', in place of the refrain ஞானப்பெண்ணே.

2568.reading: If you have not left the gross, you cannot see the subtle within it; if you climb onto the bridge and walk, is this not the great path, jnana girl?
2568.nuance: Picks up the 'gross guise' of 2567 as தூலம், the gross body, which must be left for the subtle (சூட்சம்) hidden in it to appear. The bridge (பாலம்) is tradition's suzhumunai, the one crossing from the lower body to the head.

2569.reading: Near the path, the great path, there is a city, and it is round; nada and song are heard there; it is the presence of the divine Lord, jnana girl.
2569.nuance: The round city where sound is heard is the inner station where nada is perceived, which tradition places at the crown or the brow; சந்நிதி (presence, the space before the shrine) continues the temple figure of chapter 136.

2570.reading: The presence: have you seen it? If you have, have you the skill to speak its tattva? Have you first crossed the three voids? Within it there are three lights, jnana girl.
2570.nuance: றரத்துவம் is read as தத்துவம். முப்பாழ், the three voids, are Tirumular's term for the emptinesses passed before the final state; the three lights within them are sun, moon and fire in the yogic reading, which 2572 confirms.

2571.reading: The circle of the three lights is the chakra; the tip of the nose is the suzhumunai; the one who sat in that circle of three lights is the guru, Anandanandi, jnana girl.
2571.nuance: The suzhumunai is placed at the nose-tip (மூக்கு நுனி), the point of the nasikagra gaze, rather than between the brows as in most Siddhar texts; 2572 then puts the fixed gaze at the brow. Nandi, Tirumular's name for the guru-Lord, is the one seated in the light.

2572.reading: Where Nandi sat is the fire-circle; the gaze fixed on the middle of the brows is the mark; the moon and the ray-sun stood in that place, jnana girl.
2572.nuance: The three lights of 2570 are now placed: fire where Nandi sits, sun and moon at the brow-centre where the gaze is held. In the cipher sun and moon are the two breaths, pingalai and idai, which meet at the brow; both the plain and the coded sense stand.

2573.reading: Is it not nada and bindu, the four wombs and the ten ...? Is it not nada and bindu, the seven kinds of birth? By nada and bindu come body and life; praise the supreme Nandi, jnana girl.
2573.nuance: Line 1 (நால்போனி தச) is damaged; நால் யோனி (the four kinds of womb) and தச (ten) are the likely words. The stanza derives every form of birth, and the body and life themselves, from nada and bindu, sound and seed, which in the Siddhars are the cosmic pair and the sexual pair at once.

2574.reading: In the place where bindu was, guru Nandi sat in state; if the mind grows clear and the letter M is placed there, that lord can be seen, jnana girl.
2574.nuance: மகாரம், the M of Om, is set in the place of bindu, which 2578 locates at the whirl (சுழி); the lord seen there is சீமான், the landlord of the estate figure, now the Lord. The practice is a placing of a letter at a body-station, as in the Subramaniar Njanam.

2575.reading: If one draws near the lord, the upper country becomes our dwelling; saying 'yes, yes', sing the kummi and reach grace-bliss, jnana girl.
2575.nuance: மேலைச் சீமை, the upper country, closes the estate figure: the tenants of the body's village become settlers in the land above. ஆமாம் (yes) is the kummi's clap of assent.

2576.reading: That is the place of bliss, that very place is the place of non-duality; praising Sadasiva who is the end of self, cross over and dance the kummi, girls.
2576.nuance: அவ்வீதம் is read as அத்வைதம் (non-duality), as the spelling அத்வீதம் in 2591 supports. தானந்தம் can be 'the end of self' or 'that end'; on the first reading Sadasiva is where the 'I' ends.

2577.reading: Jnana is the seat of a thousand and eight petals; the gaze is the house of the moon; silence sat there as the letter M; kindle that silence and dance the kummi, girls.
2577.nuance: The crown lotus is given 1,008 petals (ஆயிரத்தெட்டு) rather than the usual thousand, a Siddhar count repeated in 2592. The moon's house is the gaze turned upward to the crown where the moon-nectar is; M, the letter of silence, is the end of Om.

2578.reading: The kundalini-breath is the letter A; at the throat of the nape is the next letter; if you place the letter M at the whirl, is this not Siva-yoga, jnana girl?
2578.nuance: The text has அகாரம் twice; the second, at the throat, must be உகாரம் (U), giving A, U and M of Om at the root, the throat and the whirl at the crown. குண்டலி வாசி joins the coiled power to the breath, as the Siddhars do: raising the breath is raising kundalini.

2579.reading: She of the Omkara pranava sound, risen everywhere, of the colour of the Soma-digit; facing the Parashakti of the humming, dance the kummi, girls.
2579.nuance: தாரல் and றீங்காரம் are the sound of Om as a hum, and Parashakti is that sound; சோமகலை, the moon's digit, gives her colour and ties her to the nectar of 2583 and 2590. ஓங்காரமான பிரணவத்தாரல் may also be 'the stream of the pranava'.

2580.reading: Puraka is thirty-two; the mind's full kumbhaka is double that; and rechaka, to tell it, is eight-twos; know that mark, jnana girl.
2580.nuance: The counts are 32 in, 64 held, 16 out, in units of maaththirai. Tirumular gives 16 in, 64 held, 32 out and calls any change of order deceit; Valaisami's intake and release are reversed. Whether this is a different school or a corruption of the kummi's text cannot be settled; the held count agrees.

2581.reading: Pingala is where the rechaka is; placing the growing puraka in the left, so as to hold it as kumbhaka in Nandi: is this not the Siva-gaze, jnana girl?
2581.nuance: Breath in by the left channel (இடம், idai), out by pingalai on the right, held 'in Nandi', the place of the guru at the brow of 2572. சிவநாட்டம், the Siva-gaze, makes the breath-hold and the fixed look one act.

2582.reading: Know it together with the letter; from the full moon up to the new moon, doing it without forgetting according to the measure, the vaasi comes under control, jnana girl.
2582.nuance: The fortnight from பௌர்ணை to அமாவாசை may be literal, a half-month of practice, or coded: the sixteen digits of the moon as the sixteen measures of the breath. மாத்திரை is the breath-unit of 2580.

2583.reading: Raise the fire with the breath, girls; carry it above the whirl and feed it nectar, girls; proclaiming 'the muladhara's place is kechari', dance the kummi, girls.
2583.nuance: கால் is wind as well as leg, so the fire at the root is kindled by the breath. The claim that the muladhara's own place is kechari, the mudra of the tongue turned up to the palate, folds the lowest centre into the highest act: raising the fire and tasting the nectar are the same movement.

2584.reading: Lean on kechari, girl; first one can know oneself, as oneself; keenly worship the foot of the root Ganapati, jnana girl.
2584.nuance: தன்னை அறியலாம் தானாக: self-knowledge comes from the practice, not from a text. The root Ganapati is the deity of the muladhara, as in the invocation (2521), so the kummi's end returns to its beginning.

2585.reading: The letter NA is Brahma; in it Narayana became the letter MA; the letter SI is the god Rudra; I will say more, hear, jnana girl.
2585.nuance: The five letters of நமசிவாய assigned to the five gods in order, NA, MA, SI here and VA, YA in 2586: a standard Saiva correspondence in which the mantra contains the hierarchy of the five functions. கிவ்வெழுத்து is a misprint for சிவ்வெழுத்து.

2586.reading: To say it: VA is Mahesvara; completing the circle, YA, the honouring, is Sadasiva; by the faultless five letters the moving and the still have been sustained, jnana girl.
2586.nuance: சராசரம், the moving and the unmoving, rests on the five letters: the mantra is the cosmos's support, not only an aid to worship. உபசாரம் (honouring, service) names YA's function, as the soul's offering of itself.

2587.reading: The maiden's letters are three; who can say them with the mouth? Join the one above, the one below and the one between, and look quickly, jnana girl.
2587.nuance: The Maiden's three-letter mantra is left unsaid, as the stanza says it must be; tradition identifies it with the Bala (Vaalai) bija or with A, U, M at the three places of 2578. The point is that it is formed by joining three body-stations, not uttered.

2588.reading: Quickly I will say it: by the three letters, spreading always, life came to be; for those who have discerned and seen, is this not the initiation that is their protection, jnana girl?
2588.nuance: சதம் is read as 'always' (சதா); it could be 'a hundred'. தீட்சை, initiation, is here the seeing of the three letters' work in life itself, and it is called a காவல், a guard, for those who have it.

2589.reading: At the centre of the Siva-chakra called initiation, fixing the goddess's letter firmly, if Siva-puja is done with vision, siddhi comes into one's hand, jnana girl.
2589.nuance: The yantra with the goddess's seed-letter at its centre is the Sri-chakra of 2557, now the object of worship; the condition is காட்சி, seeing, which the song has required at every step. Siddhi, the practice's attainment, is promised as a thing held.

2590.reading: Do not drink toddy and reel about; do not take the sleep of ganja; feed from within on the drink of the Soma-digit and the rest, and dance the kummi, girls.
2590.nuance: The intoxicants are refused not for morals but for a better drink: the moon-nectar of the crown. The stanza takes a position on the Siddhar use of ganja, which other works mention, by naming its sleep as the obstacle.

2591.reading: Kummi-dancing girls, join the Lord of the hall and drink the nectar, girls; sing the non-duality that stands without saying 'am' or 'mum', jnana girl.
2591.nuance: அம்பலத்தையர் is the Lord of the hall, Nataraja; அத்வீதம் is advaita. The non-duality is 'sung' and yet stands without a murmur (அம், மும், the sounds of hesitation), so the song's last word on its own singing is silence.

2592.reading: ... is the beginning, girl; doing puja to the moon's thousand and eight petals, feed daily the Soma-milk that gives release, and dance the kummi, girls.
2592.nuance: The first line (அக்லீதமாவத்துக்காதியடி) is garbled; அத்வீதம் from 2591 may be in it. The puja to the 1,008-petalled moon-lotus is the inner worship of the crown, and the Soma-milk the nectar of 2590; the chapter closes with daily practice.

links.note: Tirumular's three voids where words cease give the experience at the end of the three; Valaisami asks whether the hearer has first crossed the three voids and finds three lights within the presence. Both place the final seeing past a threefold emptiness.

Tirumular puts the Lord's dwelling three or four finger-breadths from the tip of the nose, past the Veda's reach; Valaisami puts the suzhumunai at the nose-tip and the guru Nandi in the circle of light there. Both locate the Lord at the nose's point rather than only at the brow or crown.

Tirumular gazes steadily between the brows and takes the place where the Supreme sits as the little hall; Valaisami's fixed mark is the gaze at the brow-centre, where sun and moon stand and Nandi sits. The same gaze at the same place, with the hall and the fire-circle as its names.

Sivavakkiyar asks the gnanis to explain how the fourfold womb and bindu settle in the banyan seed and arise from the womb; Valaisami answers in the same terms, that the four wombs and the seven births are nada and bindu, and body and life come from them.

The Subramaniar Njanam has the two letters and the one letter moving as the ajapa in the root, sprouting from the seed-letter; Valaisami gives A at the kundalini-breath, the next letter at the throat and M at the whirl. Both distribute the letters of Om along the body's rise.

Tirumular fixes puraka at sixteen, kumbhaka at sixty-four and rechaka at thirty-two, and says to change the order in any of these is deceit. Valaisami gives puraka thirty-two and rechaka sixteen, reversing the intake and release while keeping the hold. If Valaisami's numbers are his and not a corruption, the two prescribe incompatible breath counts, and Tirumular's own rule condemns the change.

Tirumular breathes in by the left and out by pingala with the hold between; Valaisami places the puraka in the left and the rechaka in pingala, held 'in Nandi'. The channel assignment is the same in both.

Tirumular's Siva-yogis kindle the fire, turn it back and raise it, and drink step by step the nectar of the full moon; Valaisami raises the fire with the breath, carries it above the whirl and feeds it nectar. The same sequence of fire raised and nectar tasted.

Tirumular ranks Brahma, Vishnu, Rudra, Maheshvara and the five-faced one, with Sadasiva common to all; Valaisami assigns the same five, in the same order, to the five letters NA MA SI VA YA. The hierarchy of gods in one is the structure of the mantra in the other.

Sivavakkiyar holds that within the five letters are the cosmos and what is beyond it and the three gods, everything contained; Valaisami says the moving and the unmoving are sustained by the faultless five letters. Both make the mantra the container of the world.

Sivavakkiyar tells devotees that the five letters and the three letters are not the thing itself. Valaisami keeps the maiden's three letters as the key but says no mouth can speak them and they are made by joining three places in the body; he moves the letters past utterance rather than denying them.

Tirumular's king should punish those who drink liquor instead of the nectar taken by binding the breath, raising the fire and holding the moon's face; Valaisami tells the dancers not to drink toddy or sleep on ganja but to feed on the moon's drink from within. The same substitution of inner nectar for intoxicants.

Pattinathar asks when, not drinking ganja, opium and toddy, he will drink the fivefold nectar; Valaisami tells the dancers to refuse toddy and ganja and feed on the Soma-digit's drink. Both set a nectar above the Siddhar intoxicants.

source_issues: 2569: the refrain is printed ஞானப்பெண்னே (ன for ண).
2570: றரத்துவம் in line 2 is corrupt, probably தத்துவம்.
2573: line 1 (நால்போனி தச) is damaged; line 3 (லுட முயிரும பர) has broken sandhi.
2578: அகாரம் is printed twice (lines 1 and 2); the second, at the throat, should be உகாரம்.
2580: the stanza ends with a stray comma after the refrain.
2585: கிவ்வெழுதே in line 3 is a misprint for சிவ்வெழுத்தே.
2576, 2577, 2579, 2583, 2590 and 2592 end in கும்மியடியுங்கடி rather than the refrain ஞானப்பெண்ணே; this is the song's own variation, not corruption.
